Write a Python function called flatten that takes a nested list and returns a flat list. For example, flatten([1, [2, [3, 4], 5]]) should return [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
reference_answer: def flatten(lst): result = []; [result.extend(flatten(i)) if isinstance(i, list) else result.append(i) for i in lst]; return result
